question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $y.$ To do this, we treat $x$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we add $5y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-y & =7-5y \\ 4x-y+5y & =7-5y+5y \\ 4x+4y & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we subtract $4x$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+4y & =7 \\ 4x+4y-4x & =7-4x \\ 4y & =7-4x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4y & =7-4x \\ \frac{4y}{4} & =\frac{7-4x}{4} \\ \frac{\cancel{4}y}{\cancel{4}} & =\frac{7-4x}{4} \\ y & =\frac{7-4x}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
